title: Sapphire Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding at Sapphire Health. Covered project scope, success criteria, timelines, security requirements (SOC2/SSO/KMS), initial integration plan (data flows, VPC), benchmarking plan for latency/cost, and next steps to share runbooks and schedule environment access. Agreement to start a 4-week pilot focusing on chat-assisted triage and internal QA assistant.
action_items: Carlos Mendes (Redwood) - Share onboarding runbook, config checklist, and pilot scope doc by 2027-01-28
Priya Patel (Sapphire) - Send current security questionnaire and SOC2 report link by 2027-01-27
Noah Kim (Sapphire) - Provide sample traffic profile and expected qps, plus a small anonymized dataset for benchmark by 2027-01-29
Ravi Shah (Redwood) - Prepare initial Dedicated capacity recommendation and cost estimate for pilot by 2027-01-30
Amanda Brooks (Sapphire) - Create service account and grant network access for Redwood test env (VPN/VPC peering details) by 2027-02-01
next_steps: Redwood to share onboarding runbook and pilot SOW
Sapphire to return security docs and network access details
Schedule technical environment setup call next week (SE + infra)
Agree pilot KPIs and baseline metrics for latency/cost/accuracy
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood CSM), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Amanda Brooks (Sapphire Head of Data), Noah Kim (Eng Manager), Priya Patel (Security), Evan Li (Product)

Summary: Kickoff for Sapphire Health onboarding to Redwood. Focus on pilot goals (chat triage + QA assistant), data residency, VPC/private deployment options, SOC2/KMS requirements, and timelines.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, um, quick intros. I'm Lena, I'm the account lead, Carlos is our CSM, Ravi is our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Amanda Brooks: Hi Amanda here, head of data, excited to get started.
[00:23] Noah Kim: Noah - eng manager, I'll own infra and integration.
[00:28] Priya Patel: Priya from security, I'll drive the security questionnaire and compliance review.
[00:34] Evan Li: Evan product, hi all.
[00:40] Carlos Mendes: Great, thanks. Goal today is align on scope, success metrics, timeline and next steps. Should be a fairly tactical kick off.
[00:52] Lena Park: High level we heard you want Redwood for two main use cases: 1) chat-assisted triage for intake teams and 2) an internal QA assistant for support engineers. Is that still right?
[01:06] Amanda Brooks: Yep that's correct. Main constraints are data residency and PII controls, and we want predictable latency under 150ms median for short prompts. Also cost is a big factor.
[01:18] Ravi Shah: Quick note - the 150ms median will depend on model choice and deployment mode, dedicated GPUs can help but quantization and batching matter. We'll capture baseline tests.
[01:30] Noah Kim: We're leaning towards private VPC peering or Dedicated in our cloud; we have restricted egress so private option preferred.
[01:38] Priya Patel: We need to validate SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs for ePHI workflows. Also retention policies - logs must be retained for 1 year and deletable on request.
[01:52] Carlos Mendes: That's totally doable. We have Private deployment options and an on-prem package in extreme cases; most customers use VPC with customer-managed KMS. We'll send the security pack.
[02:05] Evan Li: Can you also share typical cost numbers for a pilot? We need to budget.
[02:10] Lena Park: Yes, we'll provide a pilot estimate - Ravi will draft a Dedicated capacity rec with cost ranges and fallback options.

[02:30] Ravi Shah: For pilot I'd recommend starting with 1-2 reserved GPU nodes depending on qps, with auto-burst for spikes. We'll set up prefix caching and batching policies to keep cost down. Example numbers: for small chat prompts, on A100-class nodes median p99 latencies can be 100-300ms depending on model and batch config.
[02:55] Noah Kim: A100 is fine, but we need to know network egress patterns and whether KV cache will require extra network hops.
[03:05] Ravi Shah: KV cache stays local to the serving nodes, except for the control plane. With VPC peering there's no public egress.
[03:14] Priya Patel: On KMS is there support for customer-managed keys? We can't use vendor-managed for PHI.
[03:20] Carlos Mendes: Yes, KMS/HSM integration supported for Private and Dedicated. We'll include KMS steps in the runbook.

[03:45] Amanda Brooks: For success criteria we propose: 1) median latency <150ms for triage flows, 2) model accuracy on our eval set > 85% for slot extraction, 3) cost below internal threshold - TBD.
[03:58] Lena Park: Good, we'll capture those as pilot KPIs. We'll also run a small baseline with your anonymized examples to give a performance and cost baseline.

[04:15] Evan Li: What's the suggested timeline? We're hoping to have pilot in 4 weeks.
[04:21] Carlos Mendes: That's achievable: week 1 access & env setup, week 2 bench & tuning, week 3 pilot run, week 4 evaluation & adjustments. So 4 weeks looks tight but possible.
[04:33] Noah Kim: We need to schedule a technical session for infra details - VPN/VPC peering, service accounts, firewall rules.
[04:40] Ravi Shah: I'll run that session; we should have the network topology and sample terraform module.

[04:55] Priya Patel: Also will need encryption in transit and at rest details, and a copy of the SOC2 cert. We'll share our security questionnaire.
[05:05] Carlos Mendes: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and the security pack to the follow-up email.

[05:20] Amanda Brooks: Who owns the pilot SOW? We need an internal PO.
[05:24] Lena Park: Redwood will draft a short SOW for the 4-week pilot and share pricing. Carlos will follow up on SOW and invoice cadence.

[05:40] Evan Li: Any blockers we should be aware of? For us it's legal sign-off and network readiness.
[05:47] Carlos Mendes: Ok, legal and security are usual gating items. We'll try to anticipate questions - we'll include redacted sample contracts and a list of required security attachments.

[06:05] Noah Kim: About telemetry - we want per-token cost and latency breakdowns per route if possible.
[06:12] Ravi Shah: Redwood Console supports token-level cost, per-route dashboards and traces. We'll enable a trial retention window and show you where to hook logs into your SIEM.

[06:30] Amanda Brooks: For data handling: do you redact PII by default, or do we handle that upstream?
[06:36] Carlos Mendes: We recommend client-side redaction for PII before sending, though Redwood can enable additional redaction pipelines if needed. We'll include patterns in the runbook.

[06:55] Priya Patel: One more - can we restrict model variants to open models only? No third-party hosted proprietary weights.
[07:01] Lena Park: Yes, you can pin models and we can limit catalog to approved open models or on-prem weights depending on the deployment.

[07:20] Evan Li: Great. Anything else on integrations? We want SSO for the console and RBAC for routes.
[07:27] Carlos Mendes: SSO via SAML/Okta supported; role mapping and route-level RBAC are supported too. We'll include sample SAML metadata in the docs.

[07:45] Lena Park: Alright let's recap next steps - Carlos to share runbook, SOC2, SOW. Priya to send security questionnaire. Noah to provide sample traffic and network contact. Ravi to prep Dedicated rec and schedule infra deep dive. Amanda to provision service account.

[08:10] Amanda Brooks: Sounds good. We're good to proceed on that timeline.
[08:15] Lena Park: Thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the action items.

End of transcript.
